messages:
Maya (PM): Pushed an updated Autoscale & Capacity mock to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/autoscale-v3. Key controls: Minimum capacity, Maximum capacity, Burst (toggle + pool selector + duration), GPU pool search, SLO slider (p95 ms) with numeric input, soft/hard guardrails. Opening thread for quick UX review.
Alex (Design): Layout feedback: group base capacity (min/max) on left, SLO control in the middle with small live cost estimator, guardrails on the right. Change label 'min instances' -> 'Minimum capacity (GPUs)'. Use pill toggle for burst and show 'Burst pool' dropdown only when on.
Priya (Frontend): A11y nits: slider must support keyboard (arrow +/-1, shift+arrow +/-10), aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow, and a visible focus ring. Numeric input beside the slider for precise edits. Don't rely on color alone for soft vs hard guardrails; add icons and screenreader text.
Diego (Infra): Quick API sketch for how burst maps to a pool (logical):
```
{"capacity": {"min_gpus": 1, "max_gpus": 8, "burst": {"enabled": true, "pool_id": "burst-az1", "cap": 3, "duration_mins": 20}}, "slo": {"metric":"p95_latency_ms","target":200}, "guardrails": [{"id":"g1","type":"soft","metric":"p95_latency_ms","threshold":250}]}
```
Soft = emit warning + annotate trace; hard = block scaling request. We'll need a small policy service to evaluate guardrails.
Sam (Eng Manager): Telemetry: emit events for edits (autoscale.update), preview_cost (autoscale.preview), and guardrail_violation. Rollout plan: feature flag -> internal 5% -> customer 25% with ops alert on spikes in hard rejections. Add versioning so we can rollback presets.
autoscale-bot: feature-flag "autoscale-capacity-v3" created -> staging.
Maya (PM): Action items: @Alex update Figma with copy changes and cost tile, @Priya mock keyboard+screenreader flows and provide a short a11y checklist, @Diego open API MR for burst pool lifecycle + guardrail service, @Sam draft telemetry schema and rollout timeline. Back to you all — design review Friday 11:00. :calendar:
